header.running_head: The Monetary Gifts that Hadhrat Umar (RA) Gave

blocks.text: to Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA). As she opened it, she was told that Hadhrat Umar (RA) had sent it for her. She remarked, "How many conquests have taken place at the hands of Umar after Rasulullaah ﷺ!" She then prayed, "O Allaah! Let me not live until the next gift of Umar comes in the coming year."[^1]
The Narration of Hadhrat Anas (RA) in this Regard

Hadhrat Anas bin Maalik (RA) says that Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) had appointed him to collect the Zakaah. However, by the time he returned, Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) had already passed away. Hadhrat Umar (RA) then asked him, "O Anas! Have you brought us some animals?" When Hadhrat Anas (RA) replied that he had, Hadhrat Umar (RA) told him to hand over the animals and to keep the money for himself. "But the money is a large amount," said Hadhrat Anas (RA). Hadhrat Umar (RA) insisted, "Take it even though it is so much." Hadhrat Anas (RA) says, "The money amounted to four thousand and I therefore became the richest person in Madinah."[^2]
Hadhrat Umar (RA) Gives a Gift to a Person Injured in the Path of Allaah

blocks.narrator: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Ubayd bin Umayr
blocks.text: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Ubayd bin Umayr reports that while people were busy taking their gifts before Hadhrat Umar (RA), he looked up and was surprised to see a man with a scar on his face. Upon enquiry, the man informed Hadhrat Umar (RA) that he had sustained the wound in a battle. Hadhrat Umar (RA) then gave instructions that the man be given a thousand Dirhams. After the money was given, Hadhrat Umar (RA) turned the money over in his hands for a while and then said, "Give him another thousand." Another thousand Dirhams were handed over. This occurred four times (so that the amount totalled four thousand). Feeling embarrassed that he was being given so much, the man left. When Hadhrat Umar (RA) asked about him, the people informed him that they felt he had left out of the embarrassment of being given so much. Hadhrat Umar (RA) then said, "By Allaah! Had he stayed, I would have continued giving him until there was not a single Dirham left. This is because the sword-wound he sustained in the path of Allaah had left a black scar on his face."[^3]
Hadhrat Ali bin Abi Taalib (RA) Distributes Wealth

Hadhrat Ali (RA) distributed things amongst the people thrice in a year. When some wealth arrived from Isfahaan, he announced, "Come early in the morning for the fourth round of gifts, for I am not your treasurer (I do not amass wealth for you)." He then distributed everything, even the ropes (that held the animals). While some people took them, others returned them.[^4]
Abu Ya'la. Haythami (Vol.6 Pg.6) has commented on the chain of narrators.
